## Puerto Vallarta — a seaside resort!

Puerto Vallarta, 885 km from Mexico City, is a coastal resort on Banderas Bay, the largest bay on Mexico's Pacific coast, in the state of Jalisco. This welcoming colonial town with cobbled streets was founded in 1851.

Today its picturesque old buildings with tiled roofs stand harmoniously beside ultra-modern hotels. Once a quiet fishing village, it is now one of the country's leading resorts.

## Puerto Vallarta — a tourism centre!

The city retains its colonial atmosphere, with white houses and red-tiled roofs lining its cobbled streets. There are several beach areas along the coast. Playa de Oro is known for its good conditions for water sports. The north of the resort has some of the best windsurfing spots, but the most popular beach is Playa de los Muertos, surrounded by restaurants and shops. Even while simply relaxing on the beach, you may see dolphins playing in the water and, from December to March, humpback whales.

## A Caribbean coast resort

Puerto Viejo is a hub on the Caribbean coast. It was founded in 1870 as a port for exporting bananas and coffee. Puerto Viejo is known for crystal-clear waters, palm trees, surfing and the captivating atmosphere of the Caribbean Sea.

You can take a jeep tour through the picturesque surroundings of the town. A visit to the national park offers another memorable experience: from glass-bottom boats you can watch the underwater world, with fish of every colour swimming among striking coral reefs.

## The many sides of Puerto Viejo

Influences from Afro-Caribbean, European and local Costa Rican cultures, along with those of more than 40 other peoples, give Puerto Viejo a distinctive atmosphere that you notice immediately. The resort has a joyful, lively feel. Beyond its beautiful beaches framed by palms and tropical forest, you can fully enjoy the beauty of the natural surroundings. Puerto Viejo is also an excellent place for snorkelling, diving and other water sports.
